title: Handling the Changes That Will Actually Break Our Apps in Android 17
excerpt: The transition to the Cinnamon Bun preview marks a significant shift in the Android ecosystem toward a Secure by Default and Adaptive by Default agenda. This update effectively retires many long-standing development shortcuts in favor of architectural modernization.

title: Building a Glowing Bottom Navigation with AGSL Shaders
excerpt: By leveraging Android Graphics Shading Language (AGSL) and Jetpack Compose, you can create a premium, interactive bottom navigation bar featuring a dynamic radial glow effect that responds to selection states with smooth animations and non-linear light falloff.

title: Exploring AGSL Effects in a Single Landing Page View
excerpt: Learn how to leverage AGSL to transcend the limitations of standard views by painting pixels with dynamic, mathematical precision directly on the GPU. This approach allows for the creation of immersive UI components—from textured backgrounds to reactive animations—while maintaining high performance.

title: Beyond Standard UI through Unlocking the True Power of Android Shaders
excerpt: Unlock pixel-perfect, high-performance effects by leveraging AGSL to bridge the gap between Kotlin and the GPU, enabling dynamic visuals that standard UI components cannot achieve. By moving beyond the limits of the CPU-based Canvas API, you can mathematically generate complex textures and animations on the fly for a buttery-smooth user experience.

title: Understanding How Orbiter Works on Android XR
excerpt: The Orbiter introduces a new paradigm in Extended Reality by moving persistent navigation and contextual tools off the main application window and into the 3D space surrounding it. This ensures content remains clutter-free while maintaining accessibility to essential controls.

title: Dive Into Spatial Panel UI in Android XR with Jetpack Compose for XR
excerpt: The Spatial Panel serves as the fundamental container for Android XR applications, breaking free from 2D screen constraints to place UI directly into a user’s environment. By leveraging Subspace and Spatial UI components, developers can create immersive, world-locked interfaces that automatically scale for readability and comfort.
